• Chief Technology Officer, as Data Protection Manager, for the data-handling terms of AI tools.
• Product Directorate and Business Analysts, for documenting the domain knowledge that AI tools need.
Main Purpose and Scope of Job:
• Increase the throughput and reliability of the NRLA development function by building the engineering platform that lets every team deliver small changes safely and often: AI-assisted development with clear guardrails, automated testing at every level and continuous integration and deployment pipelines for every product.
• The role is an enabling role in the Team Topologies sense. It does not deliver features and it does not take work off teams indefinitely. It works alongside each team for a defined period, builds the capability with them, hands it over and moves on. Success is measured by the four key delivery metrics moving per product, by the review queue shrinking and by teams owning the practices without further help.
Duties and Key Responsibilities
AI-Assisted Development:
• Own and maintain the AI-assisted development working agreement: approved tools, what may be shared, review expectations and how agent context is documented. Review it quarterly with the team.
• Evaluate AI coding, review and testing tools against NRLA needs, run time-boxed trials, and recommend what to adopt, what to drop and what the budget should be.
• Design the agent context files, prompts and workflows for each repository with the team that owns it, and keep them in version control alongside the code.
• Work with Product and the BAs to get the domain knowledge that AI tools depend on out of people’s heads and into documentation that agents and new joiners can use.
• Coach developers and QA in prompting, supervising and evaluating AI-generated code, and in designing software that AI tools can work on safely.
• Measure the effect of AI tooling on the four key metrics and on quality, and report it to the Deputy Director monthly.
Test Automation:
• Design the test automation strategy for each product with its team: unit, integration, contract and end-to-end tests, and the test data management that lets them run reliably on every change.
• Build the first automated test suites and CI test stages with the team, then hand over ownership. Use AI tooling to generate and maintain tests where it is reliable, and say where it is not.
• Work with the QA specialists to move testing earlier in the development cycle and to reduce manual regression testing before release.
• Agree a definition of done that includes automated tests, and help teams meet it.
CI/CD Pipelines:
• Design and build the continuous integration and deployment pipelines for every NRLA product, so that each change is built, tested and scanned automatically and releasing to production is a merge or a single action.
• Agree with the DevOps Manager which environments, runners and infrastructure services the pipelines depend on, and who provides them.
• Build dependency scanning, secrets detection, licence checks and static analysis into the pipeline, and set the observability minimums (logging, monitoring, alerting, error-to-ticket flow) for each product.
• Remove the manual steps between a change being finished and being live, and measure the lead time that results.
Enablement and Handover:
• Work with one or two teams at a time for an agreed period, in the facilitating interaction mode, with a written statement of what capability the team will own at the end and a date.
• Run the standing AI and engineering practice slot at the fortnightly engineering community session.
• Support the integration of acquired development teams by bringing their codebases onto the same pipelines, test standards and AI working agreement from their first quarter.
• Document everything built so that no pipeline, test suite or tool depends on this role to keep running.
Delivery Performance:
• Help the Deputy Director baseline the four key delivery metrics per product in October 2026 and automate their collection from Git, CI and Jira.
• Analyse where time goes between a change being written and being live, and propose the improvements with the largest payback for each team.
• Protect the review queue: track pull request size and review turnaround, and work with teams to keep both within the agreed norms.
Security, Data Protection and Compliance:
• Apply NRLA’s information governance standards to every tool and pipeline, and raise data protection questions with the CTO before, not after, a tool is used.
• Comply with NRLA policy and statutory requirements, including data protection, information security, equality and diversity, health and safety and the code of conduct.
Person Specification
Qualifications:
• Degree in computer science, engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
• Cloud (GCP), DevOps or security certifications (desirable).
Skills and Abilities:
• Uses AI coding assistants and agentic tools well on real codebases, understands their limits, and can set guardrails others will follow.
• Designs and builds CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions or similar) and automated test suites, and coaches developers to own them.
• Explains technical choices to developers, QA, product managers and senior leaders without line authority, and brings people with them.
• Works with one team at a time to a defined handover, resists becoming the permanent owner of what has been built, and documents as it goes.
• Measures the effect of a change rather than asserting it, and changes course when the data says so.
Experience:
• At least four years of professional software development, including hands-on CI/CD, test automation and DevOps work on production systems.
• Has introduced AI-assisted development tools into a team’s day-to-day work and can describe the results, including what did not work.
• Has built or substantially improved automated test coverage and deployment pipelines for an existing codebase.
• Experience with Angular, TypeScript, Firebase and Google Cloud Platform, or Laravel and PHP; experience across both stacks is desirable.
• Observability and security tooling in a pipeline (Sentry, OpenTelemetry, dependency and secrets scanning) (desirable).
• Coaching or enabling other developers as part of a previous role (desirable).
Knowledge:
• Modern software engineering practice: continuous delivery, trunk-based development, small batches, test automation and loosely coupled architecture.
• The four key delivery metrics and the Accelerate capabilities, and how an enabling team works in Team Topologies.
• Current AI development tools and agent frameworks, how to document context for them, and the data, licensing and quality risks they carry.
• UK GDPR and data protection by design as they apply to development tooling and test data.
Personal Attributes and Other Requirements:
• Hands on, and happy to pair with developers at every level.
• Curious about new tools and disciplined about adopting them.
• Patient with teams that move at different speeds, and clear about why the pace is set where it is. • Takes ownership of outcomes, not of territory.

About Nscale
Nscale is the GPU cloud engineered for AI. We provide cost-effective, high-performance infrastructure for AI start-ups and large enterprise customers. Nscale enables AI-focused companies to achieve superior results by reducing the complexity of AI development. Our GPU cloud bolsters technical capabilities and directly supports strategic business outcomes, including cost management, rapid innovation, and environmental responsibility.
We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency. As an Nscaler, you’ll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work. If you join our team, you’ll be contributing to building the technology that powers the future.
About the Role
We're hiring a Senior Detection & Response Engineer in Cyber Defense to decide what Nscale detects, command incident response, and automate recurring security work across enterprise, cloud, production, data centre, and operational technology environments.
You'll work with engineering, infrastructure, and service owners in a three-person regional rotation: roughly one operational week followed by two weeks focused on engineering and preparedness. In-house AI agents handle level 0 and level 1 around the clock; a managed provider covers weekends and escalates in defined circumstances. We're building follow-the-sun coverage across three regional hubs. Until every hub is staffed, the rotation includes out-of-hours on-call; the intended end state is conventional weekday hours in each region without night-time paging.
This team owns detection engineering as well as response. Agents draft detection logic; you validate it and decide what goes live. Your mandate is to contain threats and fix recurring problems at their source, with success measured by the share of escalations permanently solved—not tickets closed.
What you'll be doing
Detection engineering
• Map detection coverage against attacker tradecraft and our environments, identifying blind spots and telemetry gaps.
• Turn incidents, threat research, coverage gaps, and recurring escalations into detection ideas, working with AI agents to build them.
• Assess agent-proposed rule logic in shadow mode before promotion: what it catches, what it misses, and how much noise it creates.
• Make the final call on production promotion and remain accountable for detection quality. You'll rarely write a query from scratch, but nothing goes live without your judgement.
• Retune or retire noisy, stale, or irrelevant detections, and build the business case for closing telemetry gaps.
Automation and platform engineering
• Automate recurring enrichment, triage, containment, case handling, and reporting.
• Improve first-tier agents so they resolve more independently and escalate with better context.
• Build response actions, integrations, and agent tooling in our internal security platform, and prove they work in production.
Incident command and preparedness
• Command security incidents: set objectives, coordinate engineering, infrastructure, and service owners, and keep leadership informed.
• Make containment decisions under time pressure, recognising what is pre-approved, what needs authority, and what could disrupt production.
• Run post-incident reviews that lead to engineering improvements.
• Design tabletop exercises and recovery tests, maintain practical playbooks, and automate steps that don't need a human.
• Ensure the evidence, access, knowledge, and authority needed for an incident are in place beforehand.
Your operational week
• Assess escalations against asset and business context, decide on a response, and execute approved containment, including device isolation, session revocation, access restrictions, blocking, and evidence preservation.
• Identify a lasting fix wherever warranted. Build detection and automation fixes with the agents, or specify control changes clearly for the owning team.
• Close cases with a security disposition, an owner, evidence, actions taken, and required follow-up.
• Hold the managed provider to our standards for evidence, analysis, routing, and closure quality.
• Classify findings as risk indicators or actionable using the SSVC model, and hand over the queue at the end of your region's working day as follow-the-sun coverage is established.
KPIs
• Share of escalations permanently solved
• First 90 days: one recurring alert class permanently resolved
• First 90 days: coverage mapped for one area and at least one gap closed
• First 90 days: first agent-proposed detections promoted and first platform feature shipped
About You
• 5+ years in detection engineering, incident response, security operations, threat hunting, security engineering, or related roles.
• Detection judgement: the ability to assess what a rule catches, what it misses, and how it will behave in production, with a focus on overall coverage.
• Fluency in modern attacker tradecraft and its telemetry, including credential theft, session abuse, phishing, malware execution, persistence, privilege escalation, lateral movement, command and control, and exfiltration.
• Working knowledge of Windows, macOS, and Linux internals, including persistence techniques and logging.
• Experience leading, or playing a central role in, a significant incident: running the bridge, setting priorities, and keeping leadership informed while maintaining the technical detail.
• Experience building in and securing public cloud environments such as AWS and GCP, plus hands-on investigations across endpoint, identity, cloud, SaaS, network, or production workloads.
• The ability to automate repeat work using query languages, scripting, APIs, or workflow automation.
• Sound containment judgement and a calm, methodical approach when facts are incomplete or contradictory.
• A willingness to challenge automated conclusions. You'll validate AI-generated analysis and detection logic rather than treating them as authoritative.
• Clear investigation records, actionable escalations, audit-ready case notes, and effective collaboration with engineering, infrastructure, and service owners.
Useful additional experience
• Operational technology, industrial control systems, building management systems, or critical facilities.
• Cloud or AI infrastructure, data centres, HPC, or other availability-sensitive environments.
• Detection-as-code, detection testing, adversary emulation, or purple teaming.
• Building, tuning, or evaluating AI agents or LLM-based security tooling.
• Responding to ransomware, identity compromise, destructive attacks, cloud intrusion, insider threats, or supply-chain incidents.
• Managing monitoring or response provider quality while keeping decisions in-house.
• Working in a follow-the-sun rotation.
What we can offer you
At Nscale, you'll find a collaborative, supportive, and innovative environment where your contributions spark real impact. We're building something extraordinary, and we want you at the core.
• Highly competitive UK compensation package (base + bonus + equity), with performance reviews every 12 months. 🚀
• Join one of the fastest-growing AI infrastructure companies — your chance to directly shape how global AI capacity is planned and deployed. ✨
• Expect a dynamic progression plan tailored to your ambitions. Grow by leading critical cross-functional initiatives and shaping capital strategy — always with our full support.
• Human-First Flexibility: We treat you as humans first. 🫶🏽 Our flexible workplace trusts Nscalers to deliver, giving you the autonomy to shape your day around life's moments.
Equal Opportunities Statement
We strongly encourage applications from people of colour, the LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, parents, carers, and people from lower socio-economic backgrounds.

Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement.
Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Our AI-first platform changes that: our agents capture requests, route approvals, onboard suppliers, flag risk and track every renewal, while anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer grounded in their own company’s data. Buying becomes painless for everyone, procurement gets a seat at the table, and our customers have saved more than 100,000 hours of manual work so far.
Companies like Spotify, PayPal, T. Rowe Price, JustEat, Adyen and S&P Global run procurement on Omnea. We’re backed by $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners and Accel, and we’ve been named the UK’s number one startup in the Startups 100, ranked 11th on Sifted’s 2026 list of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, and recognised as one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies.
Talent density matters more to us than almost anything else. We keep the bar high in every team, so everyone here has real ownership and real impact. Our team is full of former founders and operators who’ve scaled unicorns, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside them.
Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here.
About the role
We're looking for a Visual Designer to own how Omnea shows up in the physical world and across marketing campaigns. You'll lead design for events, print and traditional media, and presentations, and support Marketing with graphic design for campaigns, content and paid ads.
Omnea now runs roughly one event every three days, across London, New York and beyond. You'll bring it in-house, raise the quality bar and build the foundations (templates, asset libraries, print specs) so every event doesn't start from scratch.
You'll work alongside our Founding Visual Designer, who owns digital (website, animations, product assets), building on a brand direction that's already set. Together you'll keep the brand consistent everywhere, from a product launch page to a booth at an industry summit, and help it evolve as we grow, pushing it into new formats, spaces and campaigns.
This is a hands-on role with a lot of ownership. You'll take briefs from Marketing and Events, shape them, push back where needed, and see them through to production.
What you'll do
Events
Design event assets end to end: booths, roll-ups, signage, badges, invites, menus, stage visuals and merchandise.
Partner with the Events team on our own events (like our Annual Summit in New York), industry conferences and customer dinners.
Build and maintain an event asset library and templates, including a self-serve starter kit so colleagues running smaller events stay on brand without a designer.
Print and traditional media
Design print collateral and out-of-home or traditional media placements.
Prepare print-ready files and work with printers and suppliers on production, quality and deadlines.
Marketing and campaign design
Create graphic design for campaigns, paid ads, social and content, working closely with Marketing and Product Marketing.
Support product launches with campaign assets, in partnership with the digital Visual Designer.
Help Marketing self-serve by growing our brand asset bank and templates.
Presentations
Design high-impact decks for events, keynotes, webinars, sales and leadership.
Maintain and evolve our slide templates so teams can build on-brand decks themselves.
Turn rough content into clear, well-structured presentations.
Brand
Apply and extend our new brand system across print and physical formats.
Raise the quality bar on customer-facing content, including guidelines for photography and filming at events.
What success looks like
First 30 days: you know the brand system inside out, you've shipped your first event assets, and you've mapped what currently goes to contractors.
First 90 days: events and print run through you, not contractors. There's a working event template library and a print spec/supplier list the team trusts.
First 6 months: colleagues self-serve the basics (starter kit, slide templates), and you spend your time on the moments that matter most.
Who you'll work with
Events: our Events team in London and New York.
Marketing and Product Marketing: a growing PMM team plus content, customer advocacy and growth.
Design: our Founding Visual Designer and the Design Director.
Leadership: occasional high-visibility requests (keynotes, board and leadership decks).
What we're looking for
Around 5 years in graphic or visual design, ideally in a B2B or in-house brand team. If you're close to that and your work speaks for itself, apply anyway.
A portfolio with real, produced events, print and campaign work, not only screens.
Strong typography, layout and colour, and confidence working within a brand system while pushing it forward.
Experience preparing print-ready files and working with printers and suppliers.
Comfortable juggling several briefs at once, pushing back on scope and keeping stakeholders in the loop.
Confident in Figma and Adobe Creative Cloud (InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop).
Strong presentation design in Google Slides and Figma Slides.
Nice to have
Basic motion design for event screens and social.
Experience art directing photography or video.
How we hire
Portfolio review by our design team.
Intro call with Talent Team (about 30 mins).
Design deep-dive: walk us through 2 to 3 produced projects.
Meet the team: Marketing and Events stakeholders.
We keep it quick and tell you where you stand at each stage.

job_description:
Quantum Engineer – Superconducting Amplifiers & RF Design
At OQC, we aren’t just theorising about the future; we’re building it. Born from a philosophy of bold innovation, we’ve successfully transitioned quantum computing from an academic dream into a commercial reality. The most exciting thing is that we’re just getting started and we’ve recently closed our £260 million Series C funding round – the largest fundraise ever completed by a quantum computing company in Europe.
The Purpose
As a Quantum Engineer specialising in Superconducting Amplifiers & RF Design, you'll develop the technologies that enable high-performance readout of OQC's quantum processors. Combining RF and microwave engineering with advanced simulation, device design and experimental characterisation, you'll turn complex technical challenges into reliable hardware solutions that help push our quantum computing capabilities forward.
The Role
Joining our Device Scaling team, you'll take ownership of developing, modelling and optimising superconducting amplifier technologies and their integration into OQC's quantum processor readout systems.
This is a hands-on technical role where you'll work across the full development lifecycle, from circuit simulation and microwave design through to device fabrication, cryogenic testing and performance optimisation. You'll have the autonomy to investigate complex challenges, make evidence-based engineering decisions and develop reusable tools and methodologies that accelerate future development.
Working closely with specialists across readout, experimental engineering, software, fabrication and packaging, you'll help translate innovative amplifier concepts into practical, high-performance technologies.
What You'll Be Working On
• Design, simulate and optimise superconducting amplifier circuits and microwave environments, using electromagnetic and circuit modelling to improve performance.
• Develop and characterise amplifier devices, investigating gain, bandwidth, noise, saturation and stability to identify and overcome performance limitations.
• Design RF and microwave networks for impedance matching, coupling, filtering, pumping and signal routing, translating technical requirements into practical hardware solutions.
• Develop physical device layouts and collaborate with fabrication and packaging teams to optimise manufacturability, integration and device performance.
• Plan and conduct room-temperature and cryogenic measurements, validating simulations, investigating discrepancies and driving evidence-based design improvements.
• Build and improve Python-based simulation, automation, optimisation and measurement tools, creating reusable capabilities that strengthen engineering workflows.
• Own technical investigations and development work packages, collaborating across teams to integrate amplifier technologies into quantum processor readout systems, document findings and share specialist expertise.
What We're Looking For
• Strong practical experience in RF and microwave circuit design, analysis and experimental characterisation.
• Experience working with superconducting amplifier technologies, superconducting circuits or closely related low-noise microwave systems.
• Proven experience developing and interpreting circuit and electromagnetic simulations, including understanding modelling assumptions and limitations.
• Experience designing, developing or characterising electronic or microwave devices, with an understanding of fabrication, packaging and integration constraints.
• Strong scientific programming skills, preferably Python, for simulation, numerical optimisation, automation and experimental data analysis.
• Experience developing or improving scientific simulation, measurement or optimisation workflows within a research or engineering environment.
• Hands-on experience using RF and microwave instrumentation to validate designs, investigate device performance and resolve technical challenges.
• Knowledge of microwave networks, impedance matching and device layout for fabrication.
• A track record of independently delivering complex technical projects or work packages, using sound engineering judgement and evidence-based problem-solving.
• Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work across specialist technical disciplines, document findings and share knowledge.
• A PhD in Physics, Electrical Engineering, Quantum Engineering or a closely related discipline, or equivalent research and development experience demonstrating the required technical expertise.
The 'Nice-to-Haves'
• Experience designing or characterising Josephson parametric amplifiers, travelling-wave parametric amplifiers or other superconducting nonlinear devices.
• Knowledge of nonlinear circuit modelling, parametric mixing or amplifier stability analysis.
• Experience developing microwave filters, broadband impedance-matching networks or related RF technologies.
• Experience working with cryogenic microwave measurement systems or superconducting quantum computing hardware.
• Experience integrating amplifier technologies into superconducting qubit readout systems.
• Experience developing shared scientific software, automated measurement systems or reusable analysis frameworks.
• Experience mentoring colleagues, providing specialist technical guidance or contributing to technical reviews.
Why Join OQC
You will join a world-class team at the forefront of the next computational era. We offer a culture of bold innovation, the chance to work with unique lab infrastructure, and the opportunity to see your work redefine the limits of computation.
Learn more about our benefits and positive work culture here: https://oqc.tech/company/careers-at-oqc/

Team Manager, Data Analytics & Business Intelligence Reports to: Head of Data Leads: an established Analytics team Location: London office, three days a week (in-person role) Why this role exists We are a multi-million-pound business where data shapes the moments that matter most, from Results Day to the contractual and regulatory returns that carry our commitments. Our Analytics team is mature and high-performing: technically excellent, highly automated, trusted with our most critical delivery, and dependable when it matters most.
So this role is not about fixing delivery. That already works, and works well. It exists because a foundation this strong can be reaching even further than it currently does. We want data to be something the business is genuinely led by, present in more decisions, more functions, and more of how the organisation runs day to day. We are hiring a leader to guide that.
You will own our Analytics strategy and lead the team that delivers it, within the wider data strategy set by the Head of Data. Your job is to take an already excellent team and extend its reach and influence across the business. What you're walking into An honest picture, because it shapes the job:
A strong, mature team. The specialists are excellent and the delivery engine is highly automated and reliable. You are not inheriting a mess to clean up. You are inheriting a capable team that is ready to be pointed outward and led somewhere new.
Critical delivery that has to land. Results Day and our contractual and regulatory returns are immovable and high-consequence. Protecting them reliably is a given, not the ambition. New capability to harness. The team's maturity is the ideal base from which to adopt new tools and ways of working, including AI, that extend what it can offer the business. Turning that potential into governed, everyday practice is yours to shape.
If leading a strong team to greater influence appeals more than rebuilding a weaker one, this is your role. Your primary mandate: drive the power and value of data further into the business In a business where data already informs decisions of real financial and reputational weight, the biggest gains now come from reach, not from efficiency the team has already won. You will:
• Get data into more decisions and more corners of the business, turning functions into fluent, habitual consumers of insight
• Make insight something the business leads with rather than checks after the fact, shaping decisions before people think to ask
• Grow demand, trust and data literacy across the business, so the pull for data increases and the team is sought out as a strategic partner rather than a service
• Speak the language of value: quantify impact, understand the cost of what the team runs, and make the commercial case for investment where it pays back
• Feed what you learn on the front line back into the wider data strategy, helping the business get ahead of its data needs rather than only answering them
Adopting new tools and ways of working, including AI, is one of the sharpest levers for the mandate above, and you won't be starting from scratch. Within the team you already have AI leads driving work on AI tooling and agents who are ahead of the curve for the organisation. Your job is not to be the source of that expertise; it is to harness and amplify it. You will give these specialists the support and the connection to real business problems that turn their work from promising into genuinely valuable, set a pragmatic view of where it pays off, and make sure it is adopted responsibly, with the governance, explainability and fairness a regulated environment demands. You don't need to be the deepest technologist in the room; you have people for that. You need the judgement to spot where their work creates value, and the credibility and influence to take it to the business and bring the team with you.
What you'll own
Analytics strategy. You set the strategy for Analytics across the business and are accountable for delivering it, nested within the overall Data Strategy: where the team invests, what it stops doing, and how it grows its value. Critical delivery. You are accountable for the team's immovable commitments, Results Day chief among them, landing reliably and to a high bar of quality and integrity. The team, and its people. You lead an established team of Analytics specialists at a range of levels, from early-career analysts to senior people ready for their next step. You lead by direction and stretch, not instruction. A core part of the role is developing each of them on their own terms: bringing the junior analysts on with structure and craft, and giving your senior people the stretch, ownership and progression that make staying and growing here the obvious choice. You own their performance, their growth, and the retention of talent this good.
The business relationship. You are the bridge between a deeply technical team and the wider business, shielding the team from noise, translating need into priorities and results into decisions, and building the senior relationships that turn Analytics from a service into a partnership.
What success looks like In your first 90 days: you understand the team, the critical delivery calendar and the stakeholder landscape; the essentials are safe in your hands; and you have a clear, credible view of where data needs to reach next. By 6 to 12 months: critical commitments including Results Day have landed reliably; data is visibly reaching further into the business, with under-engaged functions starting to pull for it; and the team has begun adopting new ways of working that extend what it can offer. Beyond the first year you are judged on outcomes: how widely and how much data is used and trusted across the business, the demonstrable value and return from what the team delivers, the reliability of critical delivery, and the growth and retention of your specialists.
What you'll bring • The credibility to lead and earn the trust of experienced technical specialists, whether you built that managing a team directly or leading experts through influence, and the readiness to lead this team directly
• Emotional intelligence and self-awareness: you build psychological safety, adapt to how different people do their best work, and lead through trust rather than pressure
• A strong track record of aligning data to business outcomes and driving its value, quantifying impact and making the commercial case
• A genuine track record of developing people across a range of levels: bringing early-career talent on, and stretching and retaining senior specialists ready for more
• Business fluency, and confident translation between business need and technical delivery
• The judgement to adopt new tools and ways of working, including AI, where they add real value, and to do so responsibly
You won't have followed one obvious path to this role, and that's fine. If you've led through product ownership and influence rather than a long line-management history, and you're ready to lead a team directly, we want to hear from you.
How you'll lead, and the culture you'll join
Ours is a warm, collaborative and people-first culture, and we care as much about how things get done as what gets delivered. You lead with empathy and emotional intelligence, build psychological safety, and create an environment where a range of working styles and strengths thrive. You pair that warmth with resolve: you can hold delivery under real pressure and have the honest conversation when it helps, without ever making it personal or making people feel unsafe. Kind and steady, not soft.
This is an in-person role. We work together from our London office on average three days a week, because this kind of team and culture is built face to face.
Inclusion, and how to apply We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team, and to creating an environment where people of every background and working style can thrive. We particularly value leaders who bring that same instinct to how they build and support their own teams. We're happy to talk about flexible working and what a sustainable version of this role looks like for you. We welcome applicants who meet most of the criteria even if they don't tick every one, and we're glad to discuss any adjustments you need in the recruitment process or the role itself. We'll talk through the team, its scope and the wider remit in detail at first conversation.

Approved requirements arrive as short PR-FAQs and PRDs; your job is to turn them into work the engineering team can build without guesswork, and to see that work through to release.You will work day to day with the engineering squad, with Data, Operations, Support and Customer Success around you. Run the backlog and the delivery process

Keep work moving through the delivery process end to end, from specification through review and QA to release, with nothing skipping a step

Track work through to release: acceptance against the criteria you wrote, release readiness, and handover to Support and Operations
Be engineering’s first call
Be the first point of contact for engineers' questions on scope and acceptance criteria, and answer them quickly
Know which questions are yours to answer and which are decisions to escalate, and escalate them promptly rather than letting work stall
Communicate progress, risks and dependencies clearly and early
Feed what you learn in delivery back into how requirements are written, so specifications keep improving
What success looks like
Engineering is never blocked waiting for a specification, an answer or a decision

• Own day-to-day security operations. Be the first point of contact for security and infrastructure questions that arrive through direct messages, IT tickets and our security mailbox. Keep a simple record of recurring questions so the team can spot patterns and improve guidance.

• Stay ahead of threats and vulnerabilities. Monitor threat intelligence feeds, work out whether we are affected by new vulnerabilities or compromised third-party packages, and work with engineering owners to get fixes made.

• Documentation others can use. Turn what you learn into short, practical runbooks for core security operations and a record of common questions and how they are best answered.
• A clearer view of risk. Start mapping our most business-critical services and the third-party dependencies behind them. Propose practical ways to measure risk and to strengthen shared ownership of security across engineering teams.

Hi 👋 I'm Mountain, Head of Technical Success at Pinpoint.
Pinpoint builds the hiring software that in house recruiting teams use to attract, hire and onboard the right people. We have a mature product, strong product market fit and a lot of happy customers.
Technical Success clears the technical path for everyone who touches a customer. When Sales, Customer Success or Implementation hits something complex inside the platform (a careers site change, a bulk data job through our API, an integration, a migration, an escalation nobody else can crack), it lands with us. We've just welcomed our first Senior Technical Success Engineer, and we're expanding how the team works around automation and AI rather than more hands on the queue. We want the next person to help build that, which is why we're hiring a second Senior Technical Success Engineer.
That's where you come in. You look at a queue of tickets and see the workflow behind them. You'd rather fix the pattern than close the ticket, you reach for AI to do it, and you check what it gives you before a customer ever sees it. You won't know every technology on day one, but you're the kind of person who figures it out.
What you should know up front
• This is a remote role, based in the UK, Spain, Portugal or Poland, with occasional in person team meetups.
• You'd report to me, inside R&D, working alongside a small team and partnering every day with Customer Success, Implementation, Sales and our engineers.
• This is not a support role. Support is reactive; this role exists to remove the reasons support gets called.
• We're an AI first team. AI writes our scripts, builds our tooling and does real work in our workflows, and we expect you to raise that bar, not just meet it.
• Pinpoint is still very much a startup. Priorities shift and not everything is defined, and we want people who do well in that.
• Our values actually matter here. We hire people who reflect them in how they work, collaborate, and make decisions.
• Take apart the repetitive work: build AI workflows, scripts and automations across careers site changes, bulk data jobs and onboarding, so the queue shrinks instead of grows.
• Solve the technical problems that block customer facing teams, from API and integration work to data migrations and platform configuration.
• Get under the hood of the platform to understand not just what a customer sees, but why it behaves that way and where the real fix lives.
• Turn recurring customer friction into clear signal for the product squads, not just a closed ticket.
• Be the technical partner in the room with customers, able to talk to their IT team and their talent team in the same conversation.
• Build alongside our first Senior Technical Success Engineer to set the standard for how the growing team works.
In practice, that means work like:
• Careers site changes, and fixing them when they break: custom application forms, tracking pixels, HTML and CSS tweaks, embeds that stop working after a customer changes their own site.
• Bulk data jobs through our API: mass updates, retagging thousands of records, cleanups and exports.
• Integrations set up and debugged: SSO, job board feeds, HRIS and onboarding handoffs, calendars, and customers' own API and webhook builds.
• Data migrations for customers moving off another ATS: mapping fields, cleaning messy exports and getting it all in clean.
• The escalations no one else can crack: the email that didn't send, the sync that failed silently, the config doing something nobody expected.
• Hands on technical work for customers: integrations, data, configuration and debugging, ideally at a B2B SaaS company.
• Something you've built with AI and still rely on: a workflow, agent or automation that took real work off your plate, not a certificate or a tool you tried once.
• Working code in Python, JavaScript or similar, enough to write and debug your own scripts that call an API, move or clean data, or automate a task, plus an understanding of what's going on underneath any no code tool you use.
• An instinct to fix the system behind a problem, not just the problem in front of you.
• Sound judgment about AI, including knowing when it's confidently wrong and when not to use it at all.
• Comfort with ambiguity, and a habit of figuring things out rather than waiting for a spec.
• Ease in front of a customer as well as under the hood. Most people are one or the other; we need both.
• Motivation to solve customers' technical problems after the sale, rather than to carry a number.
• Bonus: a background in technical support or support engineering where you outgrew the ticket queue and started building your way out of it.
You may not enjoy this role if
• Your AI experience is a course and a forked repo rather than something you built and use.
• You want to stay heads down and never speak to a customer.
• You need every problem to come with a documented answer before you'll touch it.
• You want to architect deep software systems all day. This role is broader and lighter touch than that by design.
We want Pinpoint to be the best place you've ever worked, somewhere you feel valued, supported and excited to grow. Here's what you get:
• Comprehensive healthcare: excellent medical, dental and vision coverage for you and your family
• Unlimited holidays: take the time you need to rest and recharge
• Mental health support: unlimited, immediate access to professional counselling via Spill
• Retirement contributions: 401k or pension contributions depending on your location
• Remote first: work where you're most productive, with flexibility and trust as the default
• Equity with real upside: share in the long term value you help create
• Fully paid parental leave: up to 16 weeks of paid leave for new parents
• Learning budget: annual funds for courses, books or anything that supports your growth
A detailed overview of our benefits is here.
What you're wondering
• Who would I report to, and who's on the team? Me, Mountain, Head of Technical Success. You'd work closely with our first Senior Technical Success Engineer and the wider TS team, and partner every day with Customer Success, Implementation, Sales and Engineering.
• Is this a new role or a backfill, and why now? It's a new seat. We hired our first Senior Technical Success Engineer in the autumn, it's working, and we're growing the team around the same idea: fewer tickets done by hand, more of the work done by things we've built.
• What does success look like in the first 90 days? You'll carry a real share of the queue, roughly 80% queue and 20% protected time to build, because you can't take apart a system you haven't worked inside. By the end of your first quarter, you'll have shipped your first automations that take a repeat job off the team's plate for good.
• What is the salary range? We'll cover pay openly in the first conversation, so nobody's time is wasted.
• Where can I be based and what hours do you expect? Anywhere in the UK, Spain, Portugal or Poland. You work 9 to 5 in your own time zone, and nobody is expected to work someone else's hours.
• How am I employed? Directly employed in the UK, and through our employer of record everywhere else.
• What tools and stack will I use? Python, JavaScript, HTML and CSS for careers site work, our own API, and AI tools to build workflows and automations (n8n and similar). You'll also lean on Pinsight, our internal AI assistant, Guru, our process library, and our engineers.

Every man needs to know about the most common cancer in men – prostate cancer. It’s a real and present danger that takes over 12,000 of our dads, grandads, brothers and friends each year.
Prostate Cancer UK is the largest men’s health charity in the UK. We have a simple ambition – to stop prostate cancer damaging lives. We invest millions in research to revolutionise testing, treatment and care. We’re blazing a trail to a screening programme that could save thousands of lives with regular, accurate tests for all men at risk. OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
• We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
• Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths. 
• Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory. 
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE Director, International Tax 
We are looking for an Director, International Tax to build and own the international tax function at Quince. This is the first dedicated tax hire in the company, and it arrives at the moment we need it most: Quince is entering Europe, Mexico, Australia, and numerous other countries on an aggressive timeline, and every one of those markets brings tax questions we do not currently have an in-house answer to.
Entity structure. Permanent establishment. VAT and GST registration. Withholding tax. Transfer pricing. Customs and import duty treatment. Local filing obligations we may not know exist until we have already tripped over them. The International Tax Director is the person who knows where those blind spots are before we walk into them, and who tells us what we need to do about them while it is still a decision rather than a problem.
The role reports directly to the VP of Accounting and functions as their right hand on anything tax — the person who can answer any tax question, or knows exactly how to go get the answer. This role is also the first call for the Head of International on any tax question tied to a new market, and a close partner to Legal, People Ops, and Supply Chain as the international footprint is built.
Responsibilities
•     Serve as the tax lead on every new-market launch — assess the tax profile of a market before we enter, flag what will and won't work, and define the registrations, filings, and structural decisions required to operate compliantly from day one.
•     Build and maintain a market-entry tax playbook and a global filing calendar, so the tenth country launch is materially faster and cleaner than the first.
•     Advise on legal entity structure and the tax consequences of each option — branch vs. subsidiary, holding structure, where IP and inventory sit, and how intercompany flows are designed — partnering with Legal on entity timing and sequencing.
•     Identify and manage permanent establishment risk created by employees, contractors, EOR arrangements, warehouses, third-party logistics providers, and local agents, including the tax implications of transitioning employees from EOR to local entity.
•     Own transfer pricing end to end: intercompany agreements, pricing methodology, master file and local file documentation, country-by-country reporting where applicable, and defense of the position under audit.
•     Own indirect tax globally — EU VAT (including OSS/IOSS, distance-selling rules, import VAT, and reverse charge), UK VAT, Mexican IVA, Australian GST and low-value imported goods rules, and the considerably more complex South American regimes — covering registration, filing, recoverability, and the operational setup behind each.
Qualifications
•     Deep international tax capability is essential given the scope of this role — cross-border structuring, transfer pricing, treaty analysis, permanent establishment, and indirect tax across multiple regimes.
•     Working knowledge of US federal and state taxation, including ASC 740, is a plus rather than a requirement. Our US provision and returns are prepared by an external firm; what we need is someone who can manage that firm credibly, review its work, and recognize when an answer doesn't hold up.
•     Genuine indirect tax depth, or a demonstrated ability to research an unfamiliar country's VAT/GST regime from scratch and return with a defensible, documented answer. Knowing how to find the right answer in a new jurisdiction matters more here than having memorized any one of them.
•     Demonstrated ability to stand up tax infrastructure where none exists, and to apply rigorous technical judgment to ambiguous, fast-moving, and incompletely specified situations.
•     Comfortable being the only tax person in the company. This role will not be hiring a team for at least 12–18 months, and in the meantime you are both the strategist and the person doing the work.
•     Proactive risk identifier. The most valuable thing you will do in this role is raise the issue nobody else knew to ask about.
•     Skilled at translating complex technical tax positions into clear business language that non-tax partners can act on with confidence.
•     Collaborative partner with a positive, solutions-oriented mindset; able to build trust quickly with Accounting, Legal, People Ops, Supply Chain, and the International team.
•     Agile and adaptable; comfortable building and evolving processes as the international footprint matures, without being constrained by legacy approaches.
•     Entrepreneurial mindset; equally comfortable setting global tax strategy and rolling up their sleeves to file a return.
•     Proactive problem-solver and self-starter; energized by ambiguity and motivated to find the right answer even when no playbook exists.
Preferred: •     Substantial international tax experience specifically — this is the center of the role, not an adjacent skill.
•     Demonstrated experience supporting a company through multi-country international expansion, including entity setup, indirect tax registration, and cross-border structuring.
•     Experience supporting direct-to-consumer, retail, e-commerce, or another goods-based business with a physical supply chain strongly preferred, including exposure to customs and import duty matters.
•     Experience selecting and managing external tax advisors across multiple jurisdictions.
•     Practical experience with tax engines (Avalara, Vertex, or similar) and ERP tax configuration preferred.

About the Role:
Remitly is building several partnership motions at once: employer partnerships, partners for high-value senders, Remitly Business integrations, and a long tail of comparison sites, publishers and cashback partners. Our model is simple. Segment GMs generate and qualify affiliate opportunities for their segment. Our Strategic Partnerships team, as the single global owner of the affiliate programme, closes the deals and manages the relationships across all segments. We need one person who owns everything between the term sheet and a partner that is live, tracked, protected and reporting.
You'll be the single owner of Remitly's affiliate platform (Impact) and the operational work needed to launch and support affiliates across every segment and market. This isn't a traditional affiliate marketing role: you won't manage partner relationships or carry a volume target. You'll decide which partners get onto the platform, get signed partners live without launch defects, and switch off partners who aren't playing fair. As partner volume grows faster than launch capacity, you'll also help Strategic Partnerships decide which partners to onboard first. You'll be measured on how fast and how cleanly partners go live, and on the integrity of the partner base. This is a 12-Month Fixed Term Contract role based in our London office (hybrid, 3 days per week onsite). You will report to the Director of Global Owned Channels.
You Will:
- Own Remitly's Impact account end to end: partner approvals, contract templates, payout rules, promo and tracking link setup, and data hygiene. Approve or reject every inbound partner against quality criteria you write and maintain, and audit the existing base so no unknown or inactive partner can earn commission.
- Review every negotiated deal at term sheet, before signature, and confirm feasibility. Confirm Impact can hold the commercial terms, the promo can be built and stacks correctly, landing page and creative capacity exists, and Customer Support is briefed. Say “not yet” when a deal can't launch as written, and write the technical requirements when it needs engineering, such as verifying employees so employer offers don't leak to the public.
- Work with Strategic Partnerships to prioritise the onboarding pipeline against real launch and support capacity. Keep a clear view of what's in flight, what's blocked and what's next, so Strategic Partnerships and segment GMs know when a qualified partner can go live.
- Take each signed partner from contract to live: tracking and promo code links generated directly in Impact, landing page and asset briefs to our Owned Channels creative team, and coordination with Global Brand where a launch uses organic social. Then end-to-end offer and URL testing so every promo works as intended, CS briefing, and a launch checklist.
- Run the review and approval workflow for partner-facing assets (affiliate websites, social channels and other placements) with Owned Channels, so nothing goes live off-brand or with a broken offer.
- Act as the technical and troubleshooting contact for partners and for Strategic Partnerships once partners are live.
- Build partner-level fraud monitoring with our I&T and AdTech teams. Cover click-to-install ratios, click-to-install timing, new-customer spikes against trailing baselines, and organic traffic falling as affiliate traffic rises. Act on alerts by suspending partners and flagging volume for payment hold, with Finance confirming.
- Give Strategic Partnerships the reporting they need to manage the programme and each partner's performance. Give segment GMs a trusted view of their segment's partners, including CAC and NPV per partner, and report monthly on platform health.
- Document runbooks and controls, and build AI workflows, so the programme never depends on one person's memory. Hand over a platform that runs cleanly and can scale with partner volume at the end of the 12 months.
- Be measured on: signature-to-live time, day-one launch defects, incident resolution time, fraud flags actioned, and partner base quality.

- 5+ years running affiliate or partner programmes on the operations, platform or technical programme management side, ideally in fintech, payments or another regulated, fraud-exposed category.
- Hands-on administration of Impact (impact.com) or a comparable platform such as CJ, Awin, Rakuten or PartnerStack, including contracts, payout rules, promo codes and tracking.
- Working knowledge of mobile app attribution (AppsFlyer or similar), including how probabilistic attribution and click flooding work and how to spot them in the data.

The Position
Healthcare is evolving, and Global Procurement is responding by continuously striving for the highest possible performance, taking innovative and strategic approaches to business and supplier partnerships. Global Procurement proactively manages the entire supplier ecosystem, making a vital contribution to improving health outcomes, reducing costs for patients and global healthcare systems, and ensuring that Roche continues doing now what patients need next.
As the Global Digital & Tech Strategic Procurement Programs Lead, you will guide a high-performing, agile team focused on accelerating procurement impact across Roche’s Digital & Technology supplier landscape. This role partners closely with Digital & Tech category leads and senior business stakeholders to shape and deliver strategic priorities. Your mandate is to lead a high-impact portfolio of strategic programmes, cost transformation initiatives (including targeted sourcing and negotiations) and targeted solutions that unlock measurable value from Roche’s technology supplier ecosystem.
The focus is not procurement technology implementation. It is strategic procurement leadership in a complex Digital & Tech environment: bringing programme discipline, commercial insight, supplier market intelligence and solution thinking to the opportunities where additional focus can materially improve outcomes for our business and category teams you partner with.
You will help Roche extract greater value from strategic supplier partnerships by identifying opportunities, challenging demand, strengthening commercial models, accelerating execution and scaling approaches that can create repeatable impact. • Lead a portfolio of high-impact Digital & Tech strategic programmes, cost transformation initiatives and targeted procurement solutions.
• Partner with Digital & Tech category leads and senior business stakeholders to understand priorities, shape demand and identify where additional procurement capability can materially improve outcomes.
• Drive cost transformation across complex technology spend areas, including major renegotiations, sourcing strategies, demand challenge, supplier model redesign and value capture.
• Extract greater value from strategic supplier partnerships through market insight, commercial challenge, stronger governance and innovative commercial models.
• Bring programme excellence, structure and pace from the start of complex initiatives, establishing clear outcomes, governance, roles, milestones and delivery cadence to increase the likelihood of successful execution and measurable impact.
• Build clear prioritisation logic for incoming demand, balancing impact, feasibility, strategic fit and available capacity.
• Coach and empower a high-performing team, creating an inclusive, high-trust environment where people can learn, challenge, experiment and grow

• You have experience leading complex strategic programmes, cost transformation initiatives or high-value commercial interventions.
• You know how to create value from strategic supplier partnerships, not only through sourcing events.
• You can partner effectively with category leads and senior stakeholders, building trust while constructively challenging demand and assumptions.
• You are confident shaping ambiguous priorities into clear opportunities, choices, governance and execution plans.
• You use data, market insight and commercial storytelling to influence decisions and build alignment.
• You balance savings, risk, innovation, service quality, supplier performance and long-term enterprise value.

Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.
Let’s build a healthier future, together.

job_description:
Your role
General - Administrative Support - M3 - GBR
What you'll be doing
What we are looking for
Corpay is currently looking to hire a Lead Product Manager within our Global Product team. This position falls under our Cross Border line of business. and is located in London, Moorgate.
Corpay operates a global payment network connecting customers to banks, clearing systems and payment schemes across multiple markets and currencies. As that network expands, we need to be able to add and enhance payment connectivity quickly, predictably and at scale.
The Lead Product Manager – Payment Network Expansion & Integrations is responsible for turning Corpay's payment network priorities into delivered capability. You will lead the Product Managers responsible for individual bank and payment rail integrations and own the overall connectivity delivery portfolio: translating priorities into an executable roadmap, driving integrations through delivery, certification and launch, and establishing repeatable integration patterns so that each new connection becomes easier than the last. Your role is to bring the priorities together into a coherent delivery portfolio and ensure Corpay can execute against them effectively. The successful candidate will combine deep payments knowledge with strong product leadership and execution discipline. They must be comfortable moving between senior stakeholder discussions and the detailed realities of bank specifications, payment messages, certification, reconciliation and launch readiness.
You will report directly to the Director of Product Management and will regularly collaborate with various internal teams globally.
How We Work
As a Lead Product Manager, Corpay will set you up for success by providing:
• Assigned workspace in our designated London (Moorgate), UK office location
• Company-issued equipment
• Formal, hands-on training
Role Responsibilities
Your responsibilities of the role will include:
1. Own the Payment Connectivity Delivery Roadmap
• Translate agreed Product, Commercial and Treasury priorities into a clear and executable connectivity roadmap.
• Maintain a single portfolio view across planned and active integrations.
• Assess proposed connectivity initiatives for delivery complexity, dependencies, capacity requirements and implementation risk.
• Provide stakeholders with the delivery and technical input required to support prioritisation and investment decisions.
• Sequence delivery based on agreed business priorities, dependencies, available capacity and execution risk.
• Ensure Product and Engineering resources are aligned against the highest-priority connectivity initiatives.
• Maintain clear ownership, milestones and delivery expectations across the portfolio.
• Provide senior stakeholders with concise and credible visibility of progress, risks, dependencies and decisions required.
2. Drive Bank & Payment Rail Integration Delivery
• Lead integrations from initial discovery and requirements through engineering delivery, bank or scheme certification, launch and post-launch stabilisation.
• Ensure individual Product Managers establish clear requirements, delivery plans, milestones and ownership.
• Work closely with Engineering, Architecture, Treasury, Operations, Compliance, Risk and external partners to resolve dependencies and drive decisions.
• Identify delivery problems early and ensure they are actively managed rather than becoming late-stage surprises.
• Challenge unnecessary complexity and bespoke implementation.
• Drive issues to resolution where delivery spans multiple teams or ownership is unclear.
• Ensure certification and partner dependencies are understood and incorporated into delivery planning.
• Ensure launches meet agreed product, technical and operational readiness criteria.
• Establish strong post-launch ownership and ensure significant issues are resolved quickly.
3. Build a Repeatable Payment Integration Capability
• Define consistent product patterns for integrating banks, payment rails and schemes.
• Work with Engineering and Architecture to develop reusable technical capabilities and abstractions wherever appropriate.
• Establish common approaches covering payment initiation and message mapping; validation; acknowledgements and payment status; returns and rejects; reconciliation; settlement; exception handling; monitoring and support; and certification and launch readiness.
• Establish reusable requirements, documentation and integration playbooks.
• Identify opportunities to automate integration, testing and certification activities.
• Ensure lessons from each integration improve the approach used for subsequent connections.
• Develop meaningful measures of integration performance, including delivery predictability, time-to-certification and time-to-live.
• Continuously reduce the time, effort and risk involved in bringing new connectivity live.
4. Lead the Payment Connectivity Product Team
• Allocate clear ownership across the connectivity roadmap.
• Establish common ways of working and expectations across the team.
• Set a high bar for requirements quality, product judgement, planning, communication and execution.
• Coach Product Managers through complex delivery, technical and stakeholder challenges.
• Ensure individual PMs understand not only their integration but how it fits into the wider Corpay payment platform.
• Create an effective operating rhythm across the team for roadmap management, delivery reviews, risk management and escalation.
• Step into critical integrations when additional seniority or leadership is required without becoming the default delivery PM for every initiative.
• Develop a team capable of handling increasing integration volume without requiring proportional growth in Product capacity.
5. Partner with Payments Product Leadership
• Identify emerging capability gaps and opportunities based on the existing connectivity portfolio.
• Provide assessment of integration complexity, dependencies, delivery options and likely investment required.
• Identify where existing connectivity or reusable capabilities could meet a requirement without another bespoke integration.
• Provide evidence from existing integrations, partner performance and operational experience to inform network investment decisions.
• Advise on the feasibility and sequencing of proposed connectivity investments.
• Translate agreed priorities into an executable roadmap.
6. Partner with Treasury
• Work closely with Treasury as new banking partners and network capabilities are evaluated and implemented.
• Translate agreed banking and network decisions into product and integration requirements.
• Ensure integrations support required funding, settlement, liquidity, account structures and operational models.
• Provide Treasury with clear visibility of integration progress, dependencies and issues.
• Work jointly with Treasury and external banking partners throughout onboarding, certification and launch.
• Ensure Product, Engineering and Treasury responsibilities are explicit throughout delivery.
7. Ensure Operational Readiness & Resilience
• Ensure new connectivity has appropriate monitoring, support processes, operational ownership and escalation paths before go-live.
• Work with Operations to establish scalable BAU processes rather than partner-specific manual workarounds.
• Ensure reconciliation, exception management and payment-status processes are understood and operationally viable.
• Use post-launch performance and incident data to identify opportunities for improvement.
• Ensure recurring operational problems feed back into the connectivity roadmap and reusable platform capabilities.
Experience & Background
• Significant product management or product delivery experience within payments, banking infrastructure or financial technology.
• Strong practical experience delivering bank, payment rail, clearing or scheme integrations.
• Experience managing multiple complex integrations or infrastructure initiatives concurrently.
• Strong understanding of the payment lifecycle, including initiation, clearing, settlement, reconciliation, payment status, returns and exceptions.
• Working knowledge of payment messaging and standards, including ISO 20022.
• Experience working directly with banks, processors, payment schemes or other network participants through integration and certification.
• Evidence of creating reusable integration patterns, processes or platform capabilities rather than repeatedly delivering bespoke implementations.
• Experience leading, coaching or coordinating Product Managers or comparable delivery professionals.
• Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills.
• Demonstrated ability to bring structure, transparency and momentum to complex delivery environments.
• Experience operating across Product, Engineering, Treasury, Operations, Compliance and Risk in a regulated environment.
• Experience working directly with Treasury, settlement or liquidity teams would be advantageous.
Critical Competencies
Execution Leadership
• Creates momentum, exposes problems early, drives decisions and holds teams accountable for delivery.
Portfolio Management
• Can manage multiple integrations as a coherent portfolio rather than treating each as an independent project.
Payments Expertise
• Understands payment rails, bank connectivity, clearing and settlement sufficiently deeply to challenge requirements and identify problems.
Platform Thinking
• Constantly looks for reusable capabilities, standards and abstractions rather than accepting bespoke implementation as the default.
Product Judgement
• Understands the customer and business rationale behind connectivity decisions and can contribute effectively to prioritisation without losing focus on execution.
Team Leadership
• Raises the capability of Product Managers around them and establishes clear ownership, standards and ways of working.
Executive Communication
• Can explain complex delivery situations simply and credibly: what is happening, why it matters, what is at risk and what decision is required.
Cross-Functional Influence
• Can drive outcomes across Product, Engineering, Treasury, Operations and external partners without relying solely on organisational authority.
What Success Looks Like
First 30 Days – Establish Control
• The complete payment connectivity portfolio is understood and visible; ownership across the three Product Managers is clear; a single prioritised delivery roadmap is established; current integration bottlenecks and recurring causes of delay are identified; delivery governance, stakeholder reporting and escalation mechanisms are operating effectively; and initial opportunities for standardisation and reuse are agreed with Engineering and Architecture.
By 3 Months – Improve Execution
• Integration delivery is materially more predictable; senior stakeholders have confidence in roadmap commitments and delivery reporting; common requirements, integration and launch patterns are being used across new integrations; delivery metrics including time-to-certification and time-to-live are established; reusable capabilities are beginning to replace repeated partner-specific implementation; and the existing Product Managers are operating effectively as a coherent team.
By 6 Months – Scale the Capability
• The time and effort required to launch new payment connectivity has materially reduced; new integrations predominantly follow established patterns and reuse common platform capabilities; portfolio delivery is predictable and transparent; Corpay can execute more payment connectivity initiatives without proportional increases in Product and Engineering effort; and the payment connectivity team has become a scalable execution capability for the wider Payments strategy.
What This Role Is Not
• This is not a fourth integration PM. The role leads the portfolio and the Product Managers responsible for individual integrations.
• It is not the owner of Corpay’s banking network strategy or banking relationships. Those responsibilities sit with Treasury.
• It is not a programme management role. Delivery discipline is essential, but the role also owns the product standards, integration model and evolution of the connectivity capability.
• It is not a purely managerial role. The person must have sufficient payments and integration expertise to get into the detail, challenge teams and personally unblock difficult problems when necessary.
The successful candidate will leave Corpay with a fundamentally better way of delivering payment connectivity: faster, more predictable, more reusable and capable of scaling with the growth of the global Payments business.

job_description:
Location: Stansted, UK
Work pattern: On-site (Monday – Friday)
Our Team
Want to work at the sharp end of how the world’s data moves? Join an ambitious and collaborative engineering team in Stansted, part of Semtech’s Signal Integrity Products group, developing the silicon that powers hyperscale data centres, enterprise networks and wireless infrastructure.
We work hand in hand with a world-renowned design group, and our culture is open, inclusive and driven by innovation. Here, validation isn’t a back-room function. You’ll design the boards, own the bench and shape the product.
Job Summary
Ready to put your PCB design skills to work on the most advanced silicon in the industry?
As a Senior Validation Engineer, you’ll design the high-speed validation PCBs used to evaluate next-generation devices, then characterise those devices in the lab at data rates of 25Gbit/s and beyond. You’ll take a design from schematic, through stack-up and layout, to bring-up and measurement, and your results will directly influence what ships.
No two weeks look the same. One week you might be defining the stack-up and controlled-impedance strategy for a new evaluation board; the next you’ll be debugging signal integrity on the bench, automating tests in Python, or presenting your findings in a validation review.
You’ll work with experienced engineers, industry-leading test equipment and a team that values your judgement. Bring the expertise; we’ll bring the silicon, the kit and the influence.
Responsibilities
• Design validation PCBs for new product evaluation using Cadence Allegro, from schematic capture and stack-up definition through to layout and release
• Apply high-speed and RF design practice, including material selection, controlled impedance and signal integrity, to boards operating at 25Gbit/s and above
• Bring up, debug and characterise RF and data comms boards in the lab
• Carry out benchtop characterisation of new silicon and write clear, accurate validation reports
• Help identify and select the right lab equipment for validating new products
• Build test automation software in Python (or similar) to make measurements faster and more repeatable
• Work closely with designers, product, test and applications engineers, and take part in validation review meetings
• Support new product design meetings and help shape how devices are tested
Minimum Qualifications
• BSc/MSc in Electrical/Electronic Engineering (EEE/ECE), or HNC/HND with equivalent practical experience
• Strong hands-on Cadence Allegro experience, covering both schematic and layout
• Proven high-speed PCB design experience: stack-ups, materials, controlled impedance and signal integrity
• Experience designing and debugging RF and data comms PCBs
• Able to stay focused and positive under pressure in a fast-paced R&D environment
• A natural team player with good communication skills
• Self-motivated and comfortable learning new tools and techniques independently
• Strong attention to detail and an analytical, creative approach to problem-solving
Preferred Qualifications
• PCB signal integrity simulation experience
• Python or similar for test automation
• Experience testing optical components, ICs or modules
• Lab measurement experience at 25Gbit/s and above
• Data analysis skills and the ability to present complex data clearly
Career Growth Philosophy
At Semtech, we believe that innovation starts with people. We’re committed to supporting your professional development through collaboration, structured learning and a culture that rewards initiative.
Our pay-for-performance culture celebrates meaningful contributions, and as a senior engineer you’ll have the scope to influence product validation, test strategy and board design practice.
Join us, and be part of a team that’s building the future of connectivity, together.

- Own customer security questionnaires and vendor security reviews, maintain our trust material, and develop our AI-assisted questionnaire tooling.
- Keep policies and the risk register current and readable, and translate upcoming obligations (DORA, EU AI Act, regional financial regulators) into concrete engineering work.
WHAT YOU’LL BRING:
- 5+ years in security engineering with hands-on AWS experience: IAM, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Security Hub, WAF, and the ability to investigate an incident from the logs up.
- Working fluency in Terraform, Kubernetes and GitHub Actions. You can read a module or a workflow and tell whether it does what the policy says.
- Python or a similar language for automating evidence collection, access reviews and alert enrichment, and comfort working with APIs and CI pipelines.
- Experience leading ISO 27001 or SOC 2 as the primary contact for the auditor.
- Experience with customer security questionnaires and vendor security reviews.
- Clear, concise written English for auditors, engineers and customers.
- You make decisions, prioritise against a roadmap, and ask for help early.
