About VulnCheck
Exploitation prevention is only as strong as the intelligence driving those efforts, and most of the industry is still running on intelligence that lacks exploit context. VulnCheck, The exploit intelligence company, delivers structured exploit intelligence on what is actively weaponized in the wild, purpose-built for the data lakes, ETL pipelines, automation, and AI and LLM workflows your infrastructure already runs on, raising the capability of everything it powers.
About the Role
Our Target and Canary Intelligence products provide unique visibility into vulnerable assets on the internet, attacker infrastructure, and attacks that leverage vulnerabilities for initial access. Target Intelligence maintains a continuously updated view of internet-facing systems — the services and versions they run, and their exposure to vulnerabilities. Canary Intelligence deploys intentionally vulnerable systems across the internet and captures real exploitation attempts as they happen.
We are looking for an experienced detection and response engineer to help scale the durable detections behind these products. These detections generate world-class, vulnerability-centric threat intelligence our customers rely on to defend themselves against exploitation activity on the internet.
You'll have wide latitude to shape how VulnCheck stays ahead of an accelerating volume of vulnerabilities - the tooling, the workflows, and the standards for detection engineering at scale. Although this is a 100% remote role, candidates must be located in or around Cheltenham, United Kingdom.
What You'll Do
• Design and direct AI-assisted, agentic detection workflows that scale coverage to an accelerating volume of vulnerabilities, with you on the loop for quality
• Author and ship network signatures and detections against internet-scale scan and probe data to identify services, versions, and whether hosts are vulnerable.
• Build detections against Canary telemetry that separate real exploitation signal from internet noise, and synthesize that signal into threat intelligence customers can act on
• Drive feedback loops into our probing and collection capabilities - identifying what data we should collect, what we shouldn't, and where coverage gaps exist
• Continuously evaluate detection quality, measuring and tuning false positive and false negative rates
• Respond rapidly when high-impact vulnerabilities drop - analyze, build coverage, ship
• Work alongside our vulnerability researchers and threat hunters to connect detection engineering with exploit intelligence
What You'll Bring
• 5+ years of experience building and shipping durable detections over network and host data
• Experience scaling detection development and continuous evaluation processes using AI and agentic workflows with humans on the loop
• A track record of researching, engineering, and validating durable detections across network and host telemetry, with a disciplined approach to false positives and false negatives
• Expertise in device fingerprinting and protocol analysis. You understand the nuances of how services manifest on the wire, and how these signals stack to passively uncover what is running behind an open port on an internet address
• Knowledge of attacker command-and-control techniques, covert channels, and exploitation artifacts — and how to identify them through network traffic analysis
• A background in host-based analysis and DFIR. You know what telemetry is worth collecting from sensors to identify exploitation activity and attacker behaviors, and how to synthesize it into high-quality, actionable threat intelligence
• Strong programming or scripting ability — you can codify detection logic so it is performant and integrates cleanly with VulnCheck’s engineering system
• Familiarity with CVE, NVD, KEV, or exploit intelligence datasets
• A response mindset — when a new vulnerability drops, you're the first to dig in, analyze it, and ship detection coverage
Preferred Qualifications
• Experience developing and tuning detections in Suricata, Snort, Zeek, or similar, and writing Nuclei templates or other scanner signatures
• Published detection research, signatures, or open-source detection content
• Experience with streaming systems or real-time data processing
• Background in high-growth or startup environments

Built on over two decades of cybersecurity experience, our team of experts understands the intricacies of vulnerabilities, their exploitation in the wild, and how to leverage this data to build more effective cybersecurity products that produce better outcomes for organizations.

Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.
We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.
Here’s what this particular role covers.
 
🛠️ About our Robotics Team
The Robotics team is responsible for bridging the gap from our model to our vehicle platforms, in order to let the model focus on making driving decisions. We aim to provide high quality data to the model for making such decisions, whilst abstracting away platform-specific aspects. We combine specialisms across the robotics domain, blending strong theoretical foundations with solid engineering practice to span the spectrum from research to production.
 
🧠 Your day-to-day
- Develop, integrate, tune, and validate control, trajectory-generation, and action-processing algorithms across different vehicle platforms, operating modes, and challenging driving conditions, ensuring robust real-world performance
- Maintain and evolve our controls software architecture that connects AI Driver outputs to real-time vehicle actuation and feedback
- Own requirements, release readiness, and in-field performance and issue triage
- Implement and maintain production-quality, latency-sensitive control software in C++ for deployment to prototype, reference and production vehicles
- Use simulation, closed-loop evaluation and on-road testing to characterize controller behaviour, diagnose performance issues and validate improvements
- Work with teams across Wayve to define controller interfaces, integrate with adjacent systems and enable new vehicle platforms and product features (Ownership through the full lifecycle)
- Define and track quality metrics (e.g., comfort, tracking error, and safety margin KPIs, and regressions against them)
- Contribute to safety artefacts: provide evidence for safety cases, work with the safety team to ensure compliance with required standards
🧩 What you’ll be working on:
In this role you will develop and improve the vehicle trajectory and motion controllers that translate the Wayve AI Driver outputs into safe, smooth and robust vehicle motion across different vehicle platforms and applications (both ADAS and AV). You’ll tackle cutting-edge challenges: developing principled controls approaches, implementing real time systems, testing in complex scenarios and refining our evaluation pipelines. This is a great chance to make an impact on the AV industry and grow alongside a focused team of passionate experts at the forefront of autonomous driving technology.
🙌 You should apply if you have:
REQUIRED SKILLS/EXPERIENCE
- Strong fundamentals in control theory, with applied experience in one or more of optimization, model-predictive control, numerical methods or dynamical systems
- Practical experience developing, tuning and validating motion control on complex real world physical systems (e.g., direct experience with mobile robotics and/or autonomous vehicles)
- Experience with test and validation discipline: unit and integration tests, simulation regression suites, closed-loop metrics.
- Strong software engineering skills, with experience building reliable production-quality systems in C++
- Experience with latency-sensitive or real-time software
- Ability to reason about and debug system-level behaviour in complex robotic systems across software and hardware
DESIRED SKILLS/EXPERIENCE
- Applied machine learning experience, or experience developing systems that integrate with ML components
- Vehicle dynamics and actuation. Steering, braking and powertrain interfaces, actuator delay models, and CAN or similar vehicle bus experience
- Experience in the automotive industry, including ADAS or vehicle controls
- Experience with safety-critical systems, validation, and relevant industry standards (e.g. ISO 26262)
- Experience with monitoring and diagnostics: Logging, fault detection, and on-platform debugging tools, ideally with experience investigating field issues
- Experience across multiple platforms or vehicles. The team supports vehicle-to-vehicle variation, such as accounting for parameter identification, calibration, and keeping one software stack across hardware variants
 
🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.
 
More about Wayve:
🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.
Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.
 
How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:
Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

Deployment Engineers own the technical side of getting Wordsmith live inside a customer.

About the role
Moorepay is building a Platform for Workforce Operations, where Payroll, HR and Workforce Management run on one data model, one workflow engine and one experience. We build it with an AI-first product and engineering operating model, and that model only works if the systems behind it work: the context our AI agents read, the tools our teams use, the data that tells us whether we are succeeding.
We're hiring a Senior Product Operations Manager to own that machinery for the Product function. This is a technical enablement role. You will build automations, run the Product Brain, design reporting pipelines and help every product person get more out of AI. Tooling administration is part of the job, and it is the smallest part.
The Opportunity:
Product strategy is set at the top and delivered by small, autonomous, cross-functional AI Pods (Engineering, QA, UX and Product), each accountable for measurable outcomes. Work moves through a structured twelve-step process, from strategy and OKRs to workstream briefs, outcome definitions, design intents and AI-ready specifications, then through build, validation and a learning loop.
That process runs on structured context. The Product Brain, our retrieval layer over the platform, domain and workstream context documents, is what our AI tooling reads before it helps anyone specify or build. If that context is stale, inconsistent or hard to find, the quality of everything downstream drops. The same is true of our tooling, our data and our ways of working.
As Senior Product Operations Manager, you own the operational backbone of the Product function. You make sure the Product Brain is accurate and well governed, the tools are joined up and automated, the reporting tells us the truth about delivery and outcomes, and every product person is confident using AI in their daily work. You work alongside our Engineering Process Lead, who owns engineering tooling and pipelines; your remit is the Product side of the operating model.
Within your first six months you will lead a time-boxed transition from a designed operating model to one that runs every day. You will run it as a phased plan, with exit criteria agreed with the CPO and oversight from a small steering group the CPO chairs.
Key Responsibilities:
• Mobilise and baseline - Audit the Product Brain and toolchain, baseline the metrics, and agree the plan and exit criteria.
• Pilot - Prove the controls, metrics and automations with a small number of pods.
• Scale and embed - Roll them out to every pod and to the go-to-market handover, and make them business as usual with clear ownership, cadence and training.
• Compliance controls and the launch-readiness framework will continue into the second half of the year, because they depend on other functions and on real launches to prove them.
• Alongside the plan you will run the change work: building capability across the function, and finding and working through resistance early.
• Own the Product Brain - Run our context RAG as a product in its own right: ingestion, structure, source precedence, freshness and retrieval quality. Make sure that what our AI tooling reads is current, accurate and traceable to an owner, with an audit trail of sources, changes and approvals so we can show what context our AI used and who signed it off.
• Govern the context hierarchy - Keep the platform, capability, domain and workstream context documents healthy, and own the standard templates for those documents and for PRPs. Track ownership and review dates, flag stale or conflicting content, and make sure updates from the learning loop actually land.
• Embed operating controls - Work with Risk and Compliance to build controls into the twelve-step process: traceability from regulatory change to the context and specifications it affects, data-residency rules for what AI context can hold and where it can be processed, and audit evidence produced as the work happens. You should be able to answer what our AI read before a statutory calculation changed.
• Lead AI adoption across Product - Be the AI capability owner for the Product function. Coach product managers, product owners and UX colleagues to use AI well, build playbooks and prompt patterns, and measure whether adoption is changing how people work.
• Build and maintain our skills and agents - Own the register of Moorepay AI skills and agents used by Product. Design, test and improve them with the people who use them, and retire the ones that no longer earn their place.
• Automate the friction out of our processes - Find the manual, repetitive steps in how Product works and remove them. Connect our tools (Aha!, Azure DevOps, Miro, Copilot and Claude) so that information moves without someone retyping it.
• Own the Product metrics framework - Define the metrics that show whether the operating model is working, across five layers: outcome, flow, quality, AI effectiveness and cost. Write the definition and data lineage for each, starting with the measures we rely on today (PRP quality and delivery scores, Kanban flow and OKR progress) and adding product usage from product analytics. Build the pipelines and dashboards that report them, and produce a quarterly board page on the operating model.
• Run the operating rhythm - Chair the weekly Product productivity review and turn its data into decisions for the CPO and Principal PMs. [To confirm: the other forums this role chairs, and the forums it prepares for.]
• Own the launch-readiness framework - Define launch tiers, the readiness checklist (operational, support, legal, commercial and customer communication), early-access design and the post-launch review. Pods and go-to-market teams own each release and each checklist dimension within it. You own the framework and automate the outputs and evidence it needs, such as release notes, marketing material and how-to guides.
• Improve the operating model - Watch how the twelve-step process runs in practice, spot where it slows down or breaks, and propose changes with evidence. Keep process documentation and onboarding materials current as the model evolves.
• Run the Product toolchain - Own the configuration, integration and governance of Product tools, including licences, access and cost. Keep this lean and automated so it stays a small part of the job.
• Co-own the seam between specification and code - Agree with the Engineering Process Lead a shared definition of the PRP handoff and one joined-up view of flow from workstream brief to release, with each side owning its own metrics. Product-side skills and agents sit with you; engineering agents and the PR-to-release pipeline sit with Engineering.
Your Authority:
• You decide - Standards for the Product toolchain, the rules for what goes into the Product Brain and which sources take precedence, template standards and metric definitions.
• You can veto - Content entering the Product Brain that fails governance, and a launch that fails the readiness gate.
• You recommend - Changes to the operating model, changes to roles, and tooling spend above budget, with the CPO deciding.
Skills & experience
We don't expect anyone to tick every box. The essentials are what matter, and we will support you on the rest, particularly compliance and launch readiness, which you will shape with our Risk and Compliance and go-to-market partners. Above all we are looking for a systems thinker who spots friction, designs the fix and measures whether it worked, and who is comfortable shaping a process that is still being refined. We are looking for someone with:
• Hands-on experience building automations and AI-enabled workflows with LLMs (Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot) and workflow tools such as n8n, Make, Zapier or Power Automate. You build things yourself and can show us examples.
